chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the male and female slave who are freed upon the master's death (mudabbars). He said: It is for their master to manumit them by writing a manumission contract (kitabah) if he wishes, and he is not permitted to sell them, unless the slave wishes to sell himself for the duration of his life, and he has the right to take his wealth if he has wealth.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.قَدْرَ حَيَاتِهِ: For the duration of his life
key_terms.يُكَاتِبَهُ: To enter into a contract of manumission

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a mudabbarr slave regarding manumission and sale according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies the master's discretionary power to convert the deferred manumission of a mudabbarr into an immediate kitabah contract, a mechanism that accelerates the slave's path to freedom. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that while the master controls the timing, the slave retains agency to sell their remaining lifespan if they possess the means, ensuring their personal wealth (mal al-rajul) is preserved for this purpose.
